Hi Elena — thanks for the questions. Below are concise answers and I attached example artifacts. Let me know if you need deeper logs or config snippets.

1) SSO / SAML
- Protocols: SAML 2.0 supported (both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows).
- Assertions: email, givenName, familyName, groups (optional). NameID: transient by default, persistent available on request.
- Signing/Encryption: Assertions are signed using our service cert; optional encryption available.
- Metadata: SP metadata is published and attached (saml-metadata.xml).
- Short note: We support both metadata URL ingest and raw XML exchange; ACS (AssertionConsumerService) endpoint is https://api.redwood.ai/saml/acs and single logout endpoint at /saml/slo.

[Attachment: saml-metadata.xml (application/xml)]

2) SCIM provisioning
- Support: SCIM 2.0 for user and group provisioning.
- Operations: Create/Update/Delete for users; create/update/delete for groups; we support bulk and incremental (PATCH with JSON Patch/delta) operations.
- Auth: Bearer token for SCIM API with scoped tokens.
- Example: attached scim-provisioning-sample.json shows a sample user create and group membership change.

[Attachment: scim-provisioning-sample.json (application/json)]

3) RBAC / least privilege
- Model: Role-based access control with predefined roles (owner, admin, engineer, billing, viewer) and custom role support for enterprise plans.
- Separation-of-duty: Role elevation is a two-step process — request via console (audit logged) + approval required from an existing admin (can configure a 2nd approver). Service accounts are constrained by token scopes.
- Evidence: attached rbac-permissions-matrix.csv maps roles to API and console privileges.

[Attachment: rbac-permissions-matrix.csv (text/csv)]

4) MFA and step-up
- MFA: Enforced for all interactive console sessions for employees and for customer administrative accounts by default on enterprise plans. Supported factors: TOTP (Authenticator apps), WebAuthn (FIDO2), SMS OTP (for recovery only).
- Adaptive: Risk-based step-up is supported for high-risk operations (role grants, key creation, export); step-up options are MFA or short-lived approval from an admin.
- Policy: summary attached (mfa-policy-summary.pdf).

Operational notes:
- Logs: All admin auth attempts and provisioning calls are logged to our audit pipeline and are retained as part of SOC 2 logs (we can provide log extracts under NDA).
- SCIM throttling: default rate limits apply; we can increase for provisioning windows.

Happy to jump on a short technical call if you want to walk through the SCIM change flows or SAML attribute mapping.

—Dev

Hi Elena — adding a couple of confirmations from product/ops side: 

- NameID: persistent NameID is available for customer-specific integrations; we enable it on a per-tenant basis after exchange of SP metadata and a short config window. We will set persistent if you need stable user mapping for downstream audit correlation.

- SCIM group delta: we support PATCH with operations 'add'/'remove' for group.members. Example PATCH (high level):
  PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/{id}
  Content-Type: application/json
  {
    "Operations": [
      {"op":"add","path":"members","value":[{"value":"user-123","display":"jsmith@example.com"}]},
      {"op":"remove","path":"members","value":[{"value":"user-456"}]}
    ]
  }

- RBAC matrix: we've attached the matrix and highlighted least-privilege defaults; by default new accounts are created with 'viewer' role and elevated via role request.
